paragraphs.text: And again he began to teach by the sea side. And there is gathered unto him a very great multitude, so that he entered into a boat, and sat in the sea; and all the multitude were by the sea on the land.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἤρξατο διδάσκειν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν. καὶ συνάγεται πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλος πλεῖστος, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἦσαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai palin ērxato didaskein para tēn thalassan. kai synagetai pros auton ochlos pleistos, hōste auton eis ploion embanta kathēsthai en tē thalassē, kai pas ho ochlos pros tēn thalassan epi tēs gēs ēsan.

paragraphs.text: And he taught them many things in parables, and said unto them in his teaching,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς πολλά, καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai edidasken autous en parabolais polla, kai elegen autois en tē didachē autou·

paragraphs.text: Hearken: Behold, the sower went forth to sow:
paragraphs.original: Ἀκούετε. ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων σπεῖραι.
paragraphs.translit: Akouete. idou exēlthen ho speirōn speirai.

paragraphs.text: and it came to pass, as he sowed, some [seed] fell by the way side, and the birds came and devoured it.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ σπείρειν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἦλθεν τὰ πετεινὰ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto en tō speirein ho men epesen para tēn hodon, kai ēlthen ta peteina kai katephagen auto.

paragraphs.text: And other fell on the rocky [ground], where it had not much earth; and straightway it sprang up, because it had no deepness of earth:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ πετρῶδες ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς·
paragraphs.translit: kai allo epesen epi to petrōdes hopou ouk eichen gēn pollēn, kai euthys exaneteilen dia to mē echein bathos gēs·

paragraphs.text: and when the sun was risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅτε ἀνέτειλεν ὁ ἥλιος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
paragraphs.translit: kai hote aneteilen ho hēlios ekaumatisthē kai dia to mē echein rhizan exēranthē.

paragraphs.text: And other fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ συνέπνιξαν αὐτό, καὶ καρπὸν οὐκ ἔδωκεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai allo epesen eis tas akanthas, kai anebēsan hai akanthai kai synepnixan auto, kai karpon ouk edōken.

paragraphs.text: And others fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing; and brought forth, thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄλλα ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν καλήν, καὶ ἐδίδου καρπὸν ἀναβαίνοντα καὶ αὐξανόμενα, καὶ ἔφερεν ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑκατόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai alla epesen eis tēn gēn tēn kalēn, kai edidou karpon anabainonta kai auxanomena, kai epheren hen triakonta kai hen hexēkonta kai hen hekaton.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν· Ὃς ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen· Hos echei ōta akouein akouetō.

paragraphs.text: And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parables.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο κατὰ μόνας, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν σὺν τοῖς δώδεκα τὰς παραβολάς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote egeneto kata monas, ērōtōn auton hoi peri auton syn tois dōdeka tas parabolas.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Unto you is given the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all things are done in parables:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμῖν τὸ μυστήριον δέδοται τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ· ἐκείνοις δὲ τοῖς ἔξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὰ πάντα γίνεται,
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen autois· Hymin to mystērion dedotai tēs basileias tou theou· ekeinois de tois exō en parabolais ta panta ginetai,

paragraphs.text: that seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest haply they should turn again, and it should be forgiven them.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα βλέποντες βλέπωσι καὶ μὴ ἴδωσιν, καὶ ἀκούοντες ἀκούωσι καὶ μὴ συνιῶσιν, μήποτε ἐπιστρέψωσιν καὶ ἀφεθῇ αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: hina blepontes blepōsi kai mē idōsin, kai akouontes akouōsi kai mē syniōsin, mēpote epistrepsōsin kai aphethē autois.

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how shall ye know all the parables?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην, καὶ πῶς πάσας τὰς παραβολὰς γνώσεσθε;
paragraphs.translit: Kai legei autois· Ouk oidate tēn parabolēn tautēn, kai pōs pasas tas parabolas gnōsesthe;

paragraphs.text: The sower soweth the word.
paragraphs.original: ὁ σπείρων τὸν λόγον σπείρει.
paragraphs.translit: ho speirōn ton logon speirei.

paragraphs.text: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; and when they have heard, straightway cometh Satan, and taketh away the word which hath been sown in them.
paragraphs.original: οὗτοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ὅπου σπείρεται ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν εὐθὺς ἔρχεται ὁ Σατανᾶς καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐσπαρμένον εἰς αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: houtoi de eisin hoi para tēn hodon hopou speiretai ho logos, kai hotan akousōsin euthys erchetai ho Satanas kai airei ton logon ton esparmenon eis autous.

paragraphs.text: And these in like manner are they that are sown upon the rocky [places], who, when they have heard the word, straightway receive it with joy;
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὗτοί εἰσιν ὁμοίως οἱ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπειρόμενοι, οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνουσιν αὐτόν,
paragraphs.translit: kai houtoi eisin homoiōs hoi epi ta petrōdē speiromenoi, hoi hotan akousōsin ton logon euthys meta charas lambanousin auton,

paragraphs.text: and they have no root in themselves, but endure for a while; then, when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, straightway they stumble.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιροί εἰσιν, εἶτα γενομένης θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζονται.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk echousin rhizan en heautois alla proskairoi eisin, eita genomenēs thlipseōs ē diōgmou dia ton logon euthys skandalizontai.

paragraphs.text: And others are they that are sown among the thorns; these are they that have heard the word,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἄλλοι εἰσὶν οἱ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπειρόμενοι· οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον ἀκούσαντες,
paragraphs.translit: kai alloi eisin hoi eis tas akanthas speiromenoi· houtoi eisin hoi ton logon akousantes,

paragraphs.text: and the cares of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αἱ μέριμναι τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου καὶ αἱ περὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι εἰσπορευόμεναι συμπνίγουσιν τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai hai merimnai tou aiōnos kai hē apatē tou ploutou kai hai peri ta loipa epithymiai eisporeuomenai sympnigousin ton logon, kai akarpos ginetai.

paragraphs.text: And those are they that were sown upon the good ground; such as hear the word, and accept it, and bear fruit, thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκεῖνοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν σπαρέντες, οἵτινες ἀκούουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ παραδέχονται καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑκατόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekeinoi eisin hoi epi tēn gēn tēn kalēn sparentes, hoitines akouousin ton logon kai paradechontai kai karpophorousin hen triakonta kai hen hexēkonta kai hen hekaton.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Is the lamp brought to be put under the bushel, or under the bed, [and] not to be put on the stand?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Μήτι ἔρχεται ὁ λύχνος ἵνα ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον τεθῇ ἢ ὑπὸ τὴν κλίνην, οὐχ ἵνα ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν τεθῇ;
paragraphs.translit: Kai elegen autois· Mēti erchetai ho lychnos hina hypo ton modion tethē ē hypo tēn klinēn, ouch hina epi tēn lychnian tethē;

paragraphs.text: For there is nothing hid, save that it should be manifested; neither was [anything] made secret, but that it should come to light.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν κρυπτὸν ἐὰν μὴ ἵνα φανερωθῇ, οὐδὲ ἐγένετο ἀπόκρυφον ἀλλʼ ἵνα ἔλθῃ εἰς φανερόν.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar estin krypton ean mē hina phanerōthē, oude egeneto apokryphon allʼ hina elthē eis phaneron.

paragraphs.text: If any man hath ears to hear, let him hear.
paragraphs.original: εἴ τις ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
paragraphs.translit: ei tis echei ōta akouein akouetō.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete it shall be measured unto you; and more shall be given unto you.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε τί ἀκούετε. ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν καὶ προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen autois· Blepete ti akouete. en hō metrō metreite metrēthēsetai hymin kai prostethēsetai hymin.

paragraphs.text: For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken away even that which he hath.
paragraphs.original: ὃς γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ· καὶ ὃς οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hos gar echei, dothēsetai autō· kai hos ouk echei, kai ho echei arthēsetai apʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed upon the earth;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν· Οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς ἄνθρωπος βάλῃ τὸν σπόρον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
paragraphs.translit: Kai elegen· Houtōs estin hē basileia tou theou hōs anthrōpos balē ton sporon epi tēs gēs

paragraphs.text: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, he knoweth not how.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθεύδῃ καὶ ἐγείρηται νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν, καὶ ὁ σπόρος βλαστᾷ καὶ μηκύνηται ὡς οὐκ οἶδεν αὐτός.
paragraphs.translit: kai katheudē kai egeirētai nykta kai hēmeran, kai ho sporos blasta kai mēkynētai hōs ouk oiden autos.

paragraphs.text: The earth beareth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
paragraphs.original: αὐτομάτη ἡ γῆ καρποφορεῖ, πρῶτον χόρτον, εἶτα στάχυν, εἶτα πλήρης σῖτον ἐν τῷ στάχυϊ.
paragraphs.translit: automatē hē gē karpophorei, prōton chorton, eita stachyn, eita plērēs siton en tō stachyi.

paragraphs.text: But when the fruit is ripe, straightway he putteth forth the sickle, because the harvest is come.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν δὲ παραδοῖ ὁ καρπός, εὐθὺς ἀποστέλλει τὸ δρέπανον, ὅτι παρέστηκεν ὁ θερισμός.
paragraphs.translit: hotan de paradoi ho karpos, euthys apostellei to drepanon, hoti parestēken ho therismos.

paragraphs.text: And he said, How shall we liken the kingdom of God? or in what parable shall we set it forth?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν· Πῶς ὁμοιώσωμεν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἢ ἐν τίνι αὐτὴν παραβολῇ θῶμεν;
paragraphs.translit: Kai elegen· Pōs homoiōsōmen tēn basileian tou theou, ē en tini autēn parabolē thōmen;

paragraphs.text: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown upon the earth, though it be less than all the seeds that are upon the earth,
paragraphs.original: ὡς κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃς ὅταν σπαρῇ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, μικρότερον ὂν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς—
paragraphs.translit: hōs kokkō sinapeōs, hos hotan sparē epi tēs gēs, mikroteron on pantōn tōn spermatōn tōn epi tēs gēs—

paragraphs.text: yet when it is sown, groweth up, and becometh greater than all the herbs, and putteth out great branches; so that the birds of the heaven can lodge under the shadow thereof.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅταν σπαρῇ, ἀναβαίνει καὶ γίνεται μεῖζον πάντων τῶν λαχάνων καὶ ποιεῖ κλάδους μεγάλους, ὥστε δύνασθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σκιὰν αὐτοῦ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hotan sparē, anabainei kai ginetai meizon pantōn tōn lachanōn kai poiei kladous megalous, hōste dynasthai hypo tēn skian autou ta peteina tou ouranou kataskēnoun.

paragraphs.text: And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ τοιαύταις παραβολαῖς πολλαῖς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον, καθὼς ἠδύναντο ἀκούειν·
paragraphs.translit: Kai toiautais parabolais pollais elalei autois ton logon, kathōs ēdynanto akouein·

paragraphs.text: and without a parable spake he not unto them: but privately to his own disciples he expounded all things.
paragraphs.original: χωρὶς δὲ παραβολῆς οὐκ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς, κατʼ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς ἰδίοις μαθηταῖς ἐπέλυεν πάντα.
paragraphs.translit: chōris de parabolēs ouk elalei autois, katʼ idian de tois idiois mathētais epelyen panta.

paragraphs.text: And on that day, when even was come, he saith unto them, Let us go over unto the other side.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὀψίας γενομένης· Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai legei autois en ekeinē tē hēmera opsias genomenēs· Dielthōmen eis to peran.

paragraphs.text: And leaving the multitude, they take him with them, even as he was, in the boat. And other boats were with him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν ὄχλον παραλαμβάνουσιν αὐτὸν ὡς ἦν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ, καὶ ἄλλα πλοῖα ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai aphentes ton ochlon paralambanousin auton hōs ēn en tō ploiō, kai alla ploia ēn metʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: And there ariseth a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the boat, insomuch that the boat was now filling.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γίνεται λαῖλαψ μεγάλη ἀνέμου, καὶ τὰ κύματα ἐπέβαλλεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, ὥστε ἤδη γεμίζεσθαι τὸ πλοῖον.
paragraphs.translit: kai ginetai lailaps megalē anemou, kai ta kymata epeballen eis to ploion, hōste ēdē gemizesthai to ploion.

paragraphs.text: And he himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion: and they awake him, and say unto him, Teacher, carest thou not that we perish?
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἐν τῇ πρύμνῃ ἐπὶ τὸ προσκεφάλαιον καθεύδων· καὶ ἐγείρουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἀπολλύμεθα;
paragraphs.translit: kai autos ēn en tē prymnē epi to proskephalaion katheudōn· kai egeirousin auton kai legousin autō· Didaskale, ou melei soi hoti apollymetha;

paragraphs.text: And he awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ εἶπεν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· Σιώπα, πεφίμωσο. καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη.
paragraphs.translit: kai diegertheis epetimēsen tō anemō kai eipen tē thalassē· Siōpa, pephimōso. kai ekopasen ho anemos, kai egeneto galēnē megalē.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Why are ye fearful? have ye not yet faith?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί δειλοί ἐστε; οὔπω ἔχετε πίστιν;
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois· Ti deiloi este; oupō echete pistin;

paragraphs.text: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν, καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ ἡ θάλασσα ὑπακούει αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: kai ephobēthēsan phobon megan, kai elegon pros allēlous· Tis ara houtos estin hoti kai ho anemos kai hē thalassa hypakouei autō;
